Subject: PulseCare MAP: token econ checks & close timeline

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a first-pass mutual action plan (attached) that pairs the POC milestones with the evaluation plan and the unit-econ checks you asked for. Key things I called out: 

- MAP milestones (high level):
  * Week 1: Data ingest & access (sample dataset, redaction checklist)
  * Week 2: Baseline eval (50 prompt set, latency/cost snapshot)
  * Week 3: Optimization (caching + batching, quantized model trial)
  * Week 4: Final POC demo + close readiness

- Cost / unit-econ assumptions included in the attachment:
  * Tokens per request: baseline 420 tokens (mean), 95th %ile 1,200 tokens
  * Model selection: open Llama-3-70B fine-tuned QC v1 (quantized option available)
  * Token price assumptions (hosted): $0.030 / 1k tokens baseline; quantized variant estimate $0.018 / 1k tokens
  * Caching: prefix/KV caching assumed to hit 25% of requests in baseline; we show sensitivity to 10–50%
  * Batching: we model steady-state batch sizes of 8 (p99 latency target) and a throughput scenario with batch size 16 for cost-only runs

- Evaluation plan: 50 focused prompts (functional + edge cases), automated eval harness (pass/fail + generation scoring), and a manual spot-check cadence tied to each run.

Attached: PulseCare_MAP_v1.xlsx (full MAP + cost tabs) and token-econ-sensitivity.csv (spreadsheet of scenarios).

Next steps: can you confirm who from procurement should be on the MAP? Also, does the 4-week timeline align with your internal deadlines for pilot approval? If useful I can create a one-page cost summary for procurement (I can have that over to you by Wednesday).

Thanks—
Sofia

Sofia — quick internal note on the assumptions Jordan flagged: 

- Caching: 25% hit rate is reasonable for templated prompts, but for the agent-assist demo we should model a lower baseline (10–15%) and show an optimized scenario (40%) if we add a prefix cache at the app layer. Include both in the one-pager.
- Batching vs latency: batching to size 8 gives the best cost/latency balance on our current Dedicated pools; p95 at size 8 is ~220–260ms depending on seq len. If they need 350ms p95 we can push batch to 12 for additional cost savings but only for non-interactive flows.
- Quantization: suggest we include a 4-bit quantized variant in the sensitivity table — typically ~30–40% cost reduction with minor quality delta for completions (need to call out hallucination risk).

I’ll draft the one-pager with Karthik and send it to you for review by EOD tomorrow.

—Ben

Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Jordan’s ask I’ve attached a concise one-page cost summary that shows: baseline tokens/$, worst-case (no cache + full baseline), and an optimized stack (25% cache + quantized model). Highlights below: 

- Baseline: $0.030 / 1k tokens, mean 420 tokens => $0.0126 / request (mean)
- Worst-case: 1,200 tokens @ $0.030 => $0.036 / request (no cache)
- Optimized (25% cache + quantized): effective $0.009 / request (model mix + cache)

Batching recommendation: use batch size 8 for live demo (keeps p95 ~240ms); recommend async batching (size 16) for batch QA/eval runs to lower cost further.

Attached: pulsecare_cost_onepager.pdf (one-page summary). I’ve also pushed the updated MAP to the shared Drive link.
